paper.title_en: The G-RWELL — A high-performance resistive MPGD for next-gen HEP experiments
paper.abstract_en: Future high-energy experiments require gaseous detectors that combine fast response, high rate capability, and operational robustness in harsh environments. To address the timing-driven requirements of the LHCb Upgrade II muon system, we developed the G-RWELL, a hybrid resistive MPGD in which a GEM preamplification stage is coupled to a standard <math altimg="si15.svg" display="inline" id="d1e378"><mi mathvariant="normal">μ</mi></math>-RWELL amplification stage. The detector was characterized through laboratory gain measurements and beam tests performed at the CERN PS-T10 beam area with muons, using a dedicated FATIC3-based readout chain. The G-RWELL extends the <math altimg="si15.svg" display="inline" id="d1e385"><mi mathvariant="normal">μ</mi></math>-RWELL operating range and reaches a core time resolutions of 3.8 ns, with respect to 5.6 ns of a reference <math altimg="si15.svg" display="inline" id="d1e390"><mi mathvariant="normal">μ</mi></math>-RWELL case. Tuning the gain of the two amplification stages, the G-RWELL achieve a single-gap efficiency above 90% within 25 ns over a broader operating region. These results establish the G-RWELL as a promising detector concept for high-rate applications requiring improved timing performance, while further optimization and tracking-oriented studies remain in progress. •The G-RWELL combines GEM preamplification with a resistive <math altimg="si15.svg" display="inline" id="d1e409"><mi mathvariant="normal">μ</mi></math>-RWELL amplification stage.•The hybrid layout improves the headline core timing resolution from 5.6 ns to 3.8 ns.•Single-gap efficiency above 90% within 25 ns is sustained over a broader operating region.
